claims.claim: In Pompeii, a victim found wearing a gold bracelet, beside a small child, was long described as a mother.
claims.source_checked: Pilli et al. 2024, Current Biology, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007 (PMID 39515325, PMC11627482), full text via Firecrawl research index
claims.note: Results, House of the Golden Bracelet: found 1974; child (Ind. 51, est. 5-6 yrs) 'apparently standing on Individual 52's hip'; 'Individual 52 was traditionally interpreted as a woman and mother, due to the association with the child, and an intricate golden bracelet ... worn on one arm'. Abstract words it differently ('a child on their lap'); 'beside' is the least specific reading and is not contradicted by either. 'Long described' = 'traditionally interpreted' since 1974 and spread via exhibitions and publicity materials (same paper).

claims.claim: Ancient DNA says it was a man, with no sign he was related to the child.
claims.note: 'All individuals were sexed as genetically male, including the presumed female adult (Individual 52)'; Table 1: Ind. 52 genetic sex M, Y haplogroup T1a1a1b2b2b1a. 'No evidence of biological relatedness, at least up to the third degree, between any of the individuals'; both 51 and 52 had nuclear data, so the test covers this pair. 'No sign' = 'no evidence' and is weaker than the paper's own Discussion ('in fact not genetically related'). Ind. 52 is an adult ('younger middle-aged'), and the paper itself calls him 'he', so 'a man' is within the source's usage; 'genetically male' (as line 4 says) would be the strictly exact wording, optional.

claims.claim: Two victims found close together, read as an embrace, were imagined as sisters, or a mother and daughter.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007 (PMID 39515325), Results, House of the Cryptoporticus; abstract
claims.note: 'two (Individuals 21 and 22) were found close to each other in what was interpreted as an embrace ... the archaeologists hypothesized that they could be two sisters, mother and daughter, or lovers'. Wording matches. Omitting 'lovers' does not make the line false, but note the DNA result does not rule out that third reading; the script never claims it does, so acceptable.

claims.claim: One of them was genetically male.
claims.note: 'The nuclear genetic analysis was successful only for Individual 22 and revealed he was male, excluding the possibility that the pair of victims were sisters or mother and daughter.' Table 1: Ind. 22 genetic sex M. Ind. 21 gave no sex result, so 'one of them' is exact.

claims.claim: The casts were made from 1863 on, by pouring plaster into the hollows the bodies left in the ash.
claims.source_checked: doi:10.1016/j.cub.2024.10.007 (PMID 39515325), STAR Methods 'Plaster casts' and Introduction
claims.note: Methods: 'In 1863 Fiorelli set up a method to realize plaster casts ... pouring liquid chalk into the voids left by the bodies in the hardened ash'. Intro: 'pouring liquid plaster into the voids left by decay of the victims' soft tissue. Since then ... 104 plaster casts ... have been produced using Fiorelli's method.' The 1914 and 1974 casts fall under 'from 1863 on'.

claims.claim: Over the years, restorers reworked some casts, possibly to make them tell a story.
claims.note: Intro: 'The casts had been considerably manipulated and likely creatively restored in the past, with stylistic variations ... reflecting aesthetic preferences of the periods in which they were made' and 'restorers who chose to enhance or alter some features of the bodies' shapes' (Pilli citing its ref. 6, the 2015 CT/X-ray work; read here only as reported by Pilli). Discussion: 'it is possible that the exploitation of the casts as vehicles for storytelling led to the manipulation of their poses and relative positioning by restorers'. 'Reworked some casts' as fact and 'possibly' for the storytelling motive both match. Placed right after the two stories, viewers may infer these two casts were reworked; the paper does not say so, but the line's 'some casts' / 'a story' keeps it within the source.

claims.claim: The DNA does not tell us who these people were. It tells us the old stories were guesses.
claims.note: Paper: interpretations were 'suggested in the absence of genetic data ... based on the shape and position of the bodies'; scholars and public were 'speculating about the identities of the victims and their potential connections'; study 'illustrates how unreliable narratives based on limited evidence can be' and warns against 'establishing new narratives'. 'Guesses' is a fair plain-English rendering of 'speculating'; 'the old stories' reads as the stories just told, all of which the paper contradicts.

claims.claim: Hook (A4): what a viewer who swipes at second two takes away from line 1
claims.note: At ~2 s the viewer has heard only 'In Pompeii, a victim found wearing a gold bracelet', which is true. The full sentence reports the mother reading as a past description ('was long described as'), not as fact, and signals revision; it does not leave the popular false version (a mother and her child) asserted. Passes A4.
